meta.title: Autumn Budget 2026
meta.statusNote: The Chancellor is expected to stand up in the Commons at around 12:30. Some measures have already been briefed out this morning.

measures.headline: Standing charges on gas bills scrapped
measures.detail: The Treasury says the fixed daily standing charge on household gas bills will go from 2027, or as soon as possible after that.
measures.impact: The charge is about £108 a year now, but the cost is expected to move into the price per unit of gas. Martin Lewis estimates around 60% of households will pay less, mostly low users, and 40% will pay more. Reports put typical savings at roughly £22 to £50 a year.

measures.headline: Cash ISA limit stays at £20,000
measures.detail: The previous plan to cut the cash ISA allowance from £20,000 to £12,000 for under-65s, due from April 2027, has been dropped. So has a plan to tax cash held inside Stocks and Shares ISAs.
measures.impact: Nothing changes. You can still put up to £20,000 a year into ISAs tax-free, all in cash if you like.

measures.headline: Small business rates relief threshold could rise
measures.detail: Pre-Budget reports suggest the threshold for small business rates relief may go up from £12,000 to around £17,000.
measures.impact: More small shops and premises could pay less or no business rates. Not confirmed yet.

measures.headline: Alcohol duty to rise with inflation (about 2p a pint)
measures.detail: Reports suggest alcohol duty will go up in line with RPI inflation (3.9%), which works out at about 2p on a pint of beer.
measures.impact: A small rise at the bar and in shops. Pubs say it adds to their costs. Not confirmed yet.

measures.headline: Tax on rental profits could rise by 2 points
measures.detail: Pre-Budget reporting suggests a 2 percentage point rise in the tax on rental income from 2027/28.
measures.impact: Landlords would pay more tax on rental profits. Some of the cost could be passed on to tenants. Not confirmed yet.

updates.title: Martin Lewis: most will pay less, but not everyone
updates.body: The money expert welcomed scrapping the gas standing charge, currently about £108 a year. He estimates around 60% of households will pay less and 40% more, as the cost moves into the price per unit. He also warned that the January price cap could rise by around 27%.

updates.title: Alcohol duty expected to rise with inflation
updates.body: Reports say alcohol duty will go up in line with RPI inflation (3.9%), adding about 2p to a pint. Pub groups warn this adds pressure on struggling venues.

updates.title: Business owners call for 'courage'
updates.body: A London bakery founder says rising minimum wage costs are putting firms off taking on trainees and apprentices, and wants the Chancellor to be bolder.

updates.title: Greens: scrapping standing charges is 'tinkering'
updates.body: The Green Party says the gas standing charge move doesn't go far enough on the cost of living.

updates.title: Fuel poverty campaigners welcome the move, with caveats
updates.body: The End Fuel Poverty Coalition calls it 'real relief' for many households but warns that some won't see savings.

updates.title: Gas standing charges to be scrapped
updates.body: The Treasury confirms standing charges on household gas bills will be removed from 2027, or as soon as possible after.

updates.title: Cash ISA cut dropped
updates.body: John Healey has scrapped Rachel Reeves's plan to cut the cash ISA limit to £12,000 for under-65s. The limit stays at £20,000.

updates.title: Expect a cautious Budget
updates.body: Room for manoeuvre is tight because of high debt costs and talk of a possible December election. Most commentators expect few big surprises.

updates.title: It's Budget Day
updates.body: The Chancellor's first priority is expected to be reassuring bond markets. The speech is due around 12:30.
